# Controlled subgroup comparison: design and static admission

**Four distinct, legal captured-cohort compositions are documented. One proposed cross-combination was already generated by the existing recombination operator.** Do not build a new subgroup generator on the claim that this combination is unreachable. The useful remaining question is whether reciprocal placement of the two known subgroup configurations improves whole-party performance and whether each subgroup's effect depends on its partner.

This is a finite comparison proposal following the request to continue research. The archive-model proposal and prior pilots remain closed. No model, search variant, fixture suite, build, native preparation or combat was executed in this scope. Adoption remains **Hold**; no stronger party is established.

## Four complete parties

A is anchor 040e; B is anchor 49f6. First and second letters select the source of slots 1–5 and 6–10 respectively. Keep owners, equipment, levels, subgroup numbering and canonical ability order fixed. The [seed-free matrix](../TestResults/balance/tower-subgroup-matrix-design-20260916/matrix.json) contains all 200 character–Essence assignments, full character contexts, exact canonical recipe identities, copy requirements and provenance.

| BB | Anchor 49f6 | Anchor 49f6 | `6825709c4bcd84b0c72c60c552530007bed67128eb518c7c721d7a0188e0172b` | 2 |

**AB already appears in the retained practical pilot**, from proposal `retained-composition-1423084687-proposal-00046`, operator `recombine`. Its recorded discovery score is **4/8**. This is historical descriptive evidence, not independent confirmation, a new measurement, or grounds to change the future gate. BA is absent from the two checked discovery archives. The duplicate search covers **128 rows /126 unique recipes** from the retained and incumbent practical pilots; it is not an exhaustive claim that BA was never proposed anywhere. Both anchors occur in both archives.

The complete four-party outcome matrix is absent from those two discovery archives, because BA has no row. Existing rows cannot supply the missing counterfactual outcome. Do not pool the two historical panels, impute BA, or score subgroup effects by mixing old and new trials.

## What the factors actually change

The first factor only exchanges Enchanted Fairy and Illusion Fox between slots **2 and 5**, preserving expedition-wide and subgroup Essence counts. The second factor changes **five assignments across slots 6, 8 and 9**. Thus these are two exact known configurations, not a broad sample of independently evolved subgroups. Starting from AA, switching the relevant factor to B makes these replacements:

| Slot | Remove | Add |
|---:|---|---|
| 2 | essence.illusion_fox | essence.enchanted_fairy |
| 5 | essence.enchanted_fairy | essence.illusion_fox |
| 6 | essence.hobgoblin_brutal_charge; essence.web_weaver_spider | essence.bark_golem; essence.spider_queen_royal_venom |
| 8 | essence.bark_golem; essence.spider_queen_royal_venom | essence.elder_treant; essence.flame_harpy |
| 9 | essence.bark_golem | essence.elder_treant_thornstorm |

AB has BB's copy requirements; BA has AA's copy requirements. Keeping a five-character configuration intact can preserve its internal support arrangement, but a shared boss state, control effects and combat timing can couple both subgroups. No assumption of independent subgroup strength is justified. An apparent effect belongs to the complete configuration and cannot be attributed to an individual Essence from this design.

For recorded binary wins on one shared panel, the first-factor effect under second group A is `p_AA - p_BA`, and under second group B is `p_AB - p_BB`. Their difference is `p_AA - p_BA - p_AB + p_BB`. Compute that interaction from each complete four-outcome vector, retaining pairing. It is descriptive under this outline; the planned promotion decision is based on the four candidate-versus-anchor contrasts below, not a post-hoc interaction-significance claim.

## Static checks and limits

The source inspection follows [canonical ordering](../LL/tools/BalanceHarness/TowerCompositionSearch.cs), [canonical hashing](../LL/tools/BalanceHarness/HarnessJson.cs) and [party legality](../LL/tools/BalanceHarness/TowerBossDiscoveryContract.cs), including exactly ten slots, five distinct allowed Essence IDs per character, and five different source families case-insensitively. Python reconstruction reproduces both anchors' existing canonical IDs. All four compositions retain the same complete non-Essence character fields and match the captured scenario templates after the scenario builder's explicit neutral-identity assignment. The initial direct comparison against raw templates failed because those identity slots were not yet populated. The [correction record](../TestResults/balance/tower-subgroup-matrix-design-20260916/template-check-correction.json), original source and failure log are retained; no context field was ignored. Their full-pool assumption is **OwnedCopies=null**; this is not a real account's inventory check.

The cohort is floor-5 Kharad, ten level-40 characters, tier 1/rank 2 Standard gear, five level-1 unascended/unevolved Essences each, neutral identities, no styles and no contributions. The handoff's source exports, captured content/settings/execution identities, the two sealed discovery sources and original outcome links were checked. **16/16 current data-file hashes match the captured content.** This is a data comparison only. No current dirty-checkout gameplay executable was built or admitted, and no native reconstruction was run. A later launch must explicitly choose and admit one executable/content cohort; matching data does not establish current-runtime parity.

The existing [recombination implementation](../LL/tools/BalanceHarness/TowerSuppliedCompositionSearch.cs) already proposed AB. The [prior feedback policy](../LL/tools/BalanceHarness/TowerGenerationFeedback.cs) also already allocates extra observations to selected parents. Consequently, this proposal should be assessed for the information supplied by a complete controlled matrix, without presenting either recombination or resampling as a missing feature.

## One later bounded comparison

The [comparison outline](../TestResults/balance/tower-subgroup-matrix-design-20260916/comparison-outline.json) proposes **4 parties ×256 shared independent outcomes =1,024 fights**, all frozen before any new outcomes are observed. There is no candidate generation, shortlist pruning, winner-only confirmation, or exploratory panel. Both anchors and both reciprocal candidates receive the entire panel. Old discovery and confirmation values remain excluded.

Predeclare all four positive contrasts: **AB−AA, AB−BB, BA−AA, BA−BB**. A candidate passes only if it exceeds **both** anchors by at least **five observed percentage points**, both simultaneous paired lower bounds are strictly positive, and its simultaneous win-rate lower bound is at least **10%**. Use the existing independently audited rate/paired-discordance calculation, after verifying the exact four-rate/four-contrast family in readiness: alpha .025 over four rate intervals and .025 over eight discordance intervals. These are the existing approximate interval methods; a fixed sample size does not guarantee enough precision to pass. Draws are non-wins. Incomplete or invalid evidence cannot pass.

If both candidates pass, report both; this family does not establish which candidate is better. If neither passes, close these two exact candidates with no extension, alternate subgroup configuration, changed metric or more samples. Report all four outcomes even when they are unfavorable. A successful finite party comparison would support retaining that measured party; it would not establish a generally superior search method, reliability across construction roots, or optimality.

## Smallest next work and stopping conditions

Prefer the existing complete-family evaluation and saved-evidence audit paths. The next readiness decision would check whether they can represent these four exact parties with no search stage, enforce the 1,024-attempt ceiling, freeze the statistical family, preserve every exclusion and verify independent reconstruction. No new optimizer abstraction is justified by this static inspection.

Stop before combat if any complete recipe or context fails admission; if the full matrix is found already measured on a suitable compatible independent panel; if the existing evaluator cannot enforce the complete family and caps within a separately approved readiness scope; or if the proposed information is not worth 1,024 fights. An old AB discovery row is not itself a complete matrix, but it rules out claiming AB as a newly discovered recipe. A full prospective execution protocol, measured readiness envelope and explicit future-value authorization would still be needed. **This document requests no fresh values and is not launch-ready.**
